title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes for Grothendieck's 1976 IHES talk on the divided-power (PD) de Rham complex, section 'Opérations sur complexes de De Rham à p.d.'.

Data. Let (S,S^+,t) be a commutative ring with a PD ideal S^+ and a marked element t in S^+. The typical case is S^+=(t)_{pd}, the PD ideal generated by t. To it is attached a simplicial object 𝒜(S,S^+,t)_* whose terms are differential graded algebras. From the page:
- (𝒜_S)_0 ≅ S.
- (𝒜_S)_1 ≅ S{X_0}[dX_0]. This is the PD de Rham complex of the PD polynomial algebra S{X_0}=S⟨X_0⟩ in one variable: S⟨X_0⟩ ⊕ S⟨X_0⟩dX_0.
- The two face maps (𝒜_S)_1 → (𝒜_S)_0 are α: X_0 ↦ 0 (X_0^{(i)} ↦ 0 for i≥1) and β: X_0 ↦ t (X_0^{(i)} ↦ t^{(i)}).

So 𝒜_S is a PD-algebraic model of the 'path/interval from 0 to t'. It is a divided-power, t-marked analogue of the simplicial cdga of polynomial forms on simplices, ∇(•,*), of Sullivan's rational homotopy theory.

Theorem. Regard 𝒜_S and 𝒜_{S'} merely as simplicial differential rings. That is, forget the grading, the filtration, the PD structure and the S-algebra structure; so a morphism may send a degree-0 element to a sum of a 0-form and a 1-form. Then morphisms φ: 𝒜_S → 𝒜_{S'} correspond bijectively to triples (φ_0, A'_1, (B'_i)_{i≥1}):
- φ_0: S → S' is the degree-0 component of φ.
- A'_1 = k_0φ_1(X_0) is the function part of the image of X_0. It lies in S'⟨X_0⟩^{++} = Ker α_{S'}, i.e. it has no constant term.
- B'_i = k_1φ_1(X_0^{(i)}) is the dX_0-coefficient of the image of X_0^{(i)}.

The triple must satisfy three conditions:
1) φ_0(t^{(i)}) = φ_0(t)^{(i)}. Grothendieck flags this '(!)': a bare ring morphism of the simplicial differential rings is forced to respect the divided powers on (t)_{pd}. This is a rigidity phenomenon.
2) β_{S'}(A'_1) = φ_0(t), i.e. Σ_j a'_j t'^{(j)} = φ_0(t). This is compatibility with the second face map; compatibility with α is built into A' ∈ Ker α.
3) A condition on α^*B'_i relative to the ideal J ⊂ S' generated by the coefficients a'_j of A' and b'_{jh} of the B'_j.

A remark begins and continues overleaf. When φ_0(t) is a regular element, J contains a regular element and (3) simplifies, apparently to B'_i = 0. In the isomorphism case the leading coefficient a'_1 is a unit; under 'cor. 5', if φ_0(T) = Σλ_iT^{(i)} with λ_1 a unit, then a'_1 ≡ 1 and is invertible.

Purpose: compute the endomorphisms and automorphisms of this PD simplicial de Rham object. This amounts to determining the 'operations' on PD de Rham complexes, presumably towards a functorial, choice-free construction of crystalline/PD de Rham cohomology in which reparametrizations X_0 ↦ A'(X_0) of the PD interval act.
errors: Condition 3 is not legible enough to verify. As transcribed ('(α^*B'_i) ∈ J') it is ambiguous: J is defined using the B'_j themselves, so the condition looks circular. The intended statement is probably a nilpotence or annihilation condition on the B'_i forced by multiplicativity, since (B dX)^2 = 0 and φ(X^{(i)}X^{(j)}) = binom(i+j,i)φ(X^{(i+j)}).

No proof is given on this page. The bijection is only plausible as stated: the degree-0 image of X_0^{(i)} must be determined by A'_1 through the PD structure, which is exactly what conditions 1–2 are meant to force. Without the definition of 𝒜_n for n ≥ 2 (on earlier pages), it cannot be checked that the 1-truncation determines φ.
The final NB is cut off and continues on the next page (TSVP).

ideas.what: Simplicial differential graded algebra built from PD de Rham complexes of PD polynomial algebras, with faces X_0↦0 and X_0↦t (a PD 'interval from 0 to t')
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial de Rham algebra ∇(•,*); integral/PD simplicial forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) in characteristic 0; integral divided-power forms: Cenkl–Porter (c. 1980s), later Karoubi and others on integral de Rham models
ideas.where_published: Only in these unpublished 1976 IHES lecture notes (cote 136)

ideas.what: Classification of morphisms of such simplicial differential rings, ignoring grading, by (φ_0, A', B'_i)
ideas.modern_name: Computation of the automorphism/endomorphism monoid of a PD simplicial cdga (reparametrizations of the PD interval)

ideas.what: Rigidity: a plain ring morphism compatible with differentials and simplicial structure automatically respects divided powers on (t)_pd
ideas.modern_name: Automatic PD-compatibility / rigidity of PD structures

ideas.what: Letting morphisms mix differential degrees (degree-0 elements may acquire 1-form components)
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms of underlying (super-)rings of dg algebras; odd nilpotent deformations

missed.claim: Grothendieck builds a divided-power, t-marked simplicial de Rham algebra, i.e. a PD analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms on simplices. He does this in the crystalline context, contemporaneously with or before Sullivan's 1977 paper and before Cenkl–Porter's integral divided-power forms. The link between crystalline PD de Rham complexes and integral simplicial cochain models seems not to be credited to him.
missed.quote: d'où 𝒜(S,S^+,t)_* et 𝒜'(S',S'^+,t')_*, qu'on considère comme anneaux différentiels simpliciaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to integral and p-adic homotopy theory (Mandell, and E∞/PD models of cochains) and to recent work comparing crystalline/prismatic cohomology with homotopy-theoretic cochain models.

missed.claim: An explicit classification theorem for morphisms between such PD simplicial de Rham objects. It includes the rigidity statement that ring maps automatically commute with divided powers, and the description of automorphisms as PD reparametrizations X_0 ↦ Σa'_jX_0^{(j)} with a'_1 a unit.
missed.quote: φ_0(t^{(i)}) = φ_0(t)^{(i)} i.e. φ_0 commute aux p.d. sur (t)_pd (!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a symmetry group of the PD path object. This bears on functoriality and choice-independence of PD de Rham / crystalline complexes, and on 'operations' on de Rham–Witt type complexes.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a genuine unpublished structural theorem, a PD simplicial de Rham object with its morphisms classified, which anticipates divided-power analogues of Sullivan's forms. However, the statement is partly illegible and unproved, and similar ideas later appeared independently in integral rational-homotopy work.
transcription_corrections: 'A'_1' is written in the image with a crossed or odd subscript (A'_♯ or A'_*); the content is the function part of φ_1(X_0).
Target of φ_1 reads roughly 'S'{X_0}[S' dX_0]' rather than '[^S dX_0]'.
Condition 3 in the image reads '(α* B'_i) ≡ 0' or similar, with a crossed-out subscript beneath; the transcribed '∈ J' is uncertain.
The margin note reads roughly 'NB dans le cas semi-simplicial(?) la condition 2) ... A'' and is largely illegible.
Last lines: 'Si φ_0(t) est [diviseur struck out] régulier de S' alors on a dans ce cas J contenant un élément régulier et les relations (TSVP)'.
